shlokas.devanagari: अथातोऽवाक्शिरसीयमिन्द्रियं व्याख्यास्यामः||१|| इति ह स्माह भगवानात्रेयः||२||
shlokas.english: We shall now expound the chapter "Avakshiraseeyam Indriyam" (Fatal signs like inverted shadow of dying person).Thus said Lord Atreya. [1-2]

shlokas.devanagari:
अवाक्शिरा वा जिह्मा वा यस्य वा विशिरा भवेत्| 
जन्तो रूपप्रतिच्छाया नैनमिच्छेच्चिकित्सितुम्||३||
shlokas.english: If the physical shadow of the individual is found to be inverted (head downwards and legs upwards), irregular or without the head, he must not be treated.

shlokas.devanagari:
जटीभूतानि पक्ष्माणि दृष्टिश्चापि निगृह्यते | 
यस्य जन्तोर्न तं धीरो भेषजेनोपपादयेत्||४||
shlokas.english: A person, having complete matting of eye-lashes resulting in absence of vision should not be treated.

shlokas.devanagari:
यस्य शूनानि वर्त्मानि न समायान्ति शुष्यतः| 
चक्षुषी चोपदिह्येते  यथा प्रेतस्तथैव सः||५||
shlokas.english: An emaciated person who is unable to close his eyes due to swollen eyelids and also accompanied by burning eyes should be considered as good as departed.

shlokas.devanagari:
भ्रुवोर्वा यदि वा मूर्ध्नि सीमन्तावर्तकान् बहून्| 
अपूर्वानकृतान् व्यक्तान् दृष्ट्वा मरणमादिशेत्||६||
shlokas.english: A person having appearance of bare lines over the scalp, whirls over eye eyebrows or over scalp which were not present before, will die certainly.

shlokas.devanagari:
त्र्यहमेतेन जीवन्ति लक्षणेनातुरा नराः| 
अरोगाणां पुनस्त्वेतत् षड्रात्रं परमुच्यते ||७||
shlokas.english: These patients (having above mentioned signs), will survive for three days, and healthy individuals (having above mentioned signs) will survive maximum for 6 nights.

shlokas.devanagari:
आयम्योत्पाटितान् केशान् यो नरो नावबुध्यते| 
अनातुरो वा रोगी वा षड्रात्रं नातिवर्तते||८||
shlokas.english: An ill or healthy individual, who does not respond to pulling or uprooting of hairs, does not survive for more than six nights.

shlokas.devanagari:
यस्य केशा निरभ्यङ्गा दृश्यन्तेऽभ्यक्तसन्निभाः| 
उपरुद्धायुषं ज्ञात्वा तं धीरः परिवर्जयेत्||९||
shlokas.english: If the hair of the individual appears to be unreasonably greasy then he should be considered as at the fag-end of his life and should not be treated.

shlokas.devanagari:
ग्लायते  नासिकावंशः पृथुत्वं यस्य गच्छति| 
अशूनः शूनसङ्काशः प्रत्याख्येयः स जानता||१०||
shlokas.english: A wise (physician) should consider (the patient) with depressed and thickened nasal ridge along with its pseudo – swollen appearance as incurable.

shlokas.devanagari:
अत्यर्थविवृता यस्य यस्य चात्यर्थसंवृता| 
जिह्मा वा परिशुष्का वा नासिका न स जीवति||११||
shlokas.english: Excessive nasal flaring or constriction, distortion in shape and extreme dryness of the nose indicate that the individual will not survive.

shlokas.devanagari:
मुखं शब्दश्रवावोष्ठौ  शुक्लश्यावातिलोहितौ| 
विकृत्या यस्य वा नीलौ न स रोगाद्विमुच्यते||१२||
shlokas.english: If the face, ears and lips become abnormally (without any visible cause) white, brown, excessively red or blue, then such a patient seldom recovers from the disease.

shlokas.devanagari:
अस्थिश्वेता द्विजा यस्य पुष्पिताः पङ्कसंवृताः| 
विकृत्या न स रोगं तं विहायारोग्यमश्नुते||१३||
shlokas.english: A patient having morbid conditions like appearance of bony white teeth, white flower shaped spots and mud like appearance over teeth cannot recover from the disease.

shlokas.devanagari:
स्तब्धा निश्चेतना गुर्वी कण्टकोपचिता भृशम्| 
श्यावा शुष्काऽथवा शूना प्रेतजिह्वा विसर्पिणी||१४||
shlokas.english: If the tongue becomes rigid, senseless, heavy, excessively coated with a thorn like fur, brown in color, dry or swollen and constantly mobile, then the patient having such signs should be considered as good as dead.

shlokas.devanagari:
दीर्घमुच्छ्वस्य यो ह्रस्वं नरो निःश्वस्य ताम्यति| 
उपरुद्धायुषं ज्ञात्वा तं धीरः परिवर्जयेत्||१५||
shlokas.english: If a person faints after a short expiration followed by a long inspiration, then he should be considered as nearing his end and must not be treated.

shlokas.devanagari:
हस्तौ पादौ च मन्ये च तालु चैवातिशीतलम्| 
भवत्यायुःक्षये क्रूरमथवाऽपि भवेन्मृदु||१६||
shlokas.english: Excessive coldness, roughness and softness in hands, legs and neck indicate the end of the life of the person.

shlokas.devanagari:
घट्टयञ्जानुना जानु पादावुद्यम्य पातयन्| 
योऽपास्यति मुहुर्वक्रमातुरो न स जीवति||१७||
shlokas.english: The person who strikes one knee with the other, throws down legs after lifting them up and frequently turns the face to one or the other side, does not survive.

shlokas.devanagari:
दन्तैश्छिन्दन्नखाग्राणि नखैच्छिन्दञ्छिरोरुहान्| 
काष्ठेन भूमिं विलिखन्न रोगात् परिमुच्यते||१८||
shlokas.english: The patient, who cuts tips of his nail by biting, clips hair by nail and writes on the ground with the help of a stick, succumbs to the disease.

shlokas.devanagari:
दन्तान् खादति यो जाग्रदसाम्ना विरुदन् हसन्| 
विजानाति न चेद्दुःखं न स रोगाद्विमुच्यते||१९||
shlokas.english: The patient who gnashes teeth while awake, cries and laughs loudly and does not have the pain sensation, does not recover from the disease.

shlokas.devanagari:
मुहुर्हसन् मुहुः क्ष्वेडन् शय्यां पादेन हन्ति यः| 
उच्चैश्छिद्राणि  विमृशन्नातुरो न स जीवति||२०||
shlokas.english: The patient, who frequently laughs and shouts, strikes the bed by feet and puts finger into the nostrils, ears and eyes does not survive.

shlokas.devanagari:
यैर्विन्दति पुरा भावैः समेतैः परमां रतिम्| 
तैरेवारममाणस्य ग्लास्नोर्मरणमादिशेत्||२१||
shlokas.english: If a debilitated patient develops disliking for such factors which, in the past, made him extremely happy, his death is imminent.

shlokas.devanagari:
न बिभर्ति शिरो ग्रीवा न पृष्ठं भारमात्मनः| 
न हनू पिण्डमास्यस्थमातुरस्य मुमूर्षतः||२२||
shlokas.english: If the neck of the patient is unable to support the weight of the head, the back, that of the body, the jaw bones, morsel of food in the mouth, this indicates his imminent death.

shlokas.devanagari:
सहसा ज्वरसन्तापस्तृष्णा मूर्च्छा बलक्षयः| 
विश्लेषणं च सन्धीनां मुमूर्षोरुपजायते||२३||
shlokas.english: Sudden fever, thirst, fainting, debility and looseness of joints points to death.

shlokas.devanagari:
गोसर्गे वदनाद्यस्य स्वेदः प्रच्यवते भृशम्| 
लेपज्वरोपतप्तस्य दुर्लभं तस्य जीवितम्||२४||
shlokas.english: If a patient suffering from lepajwara i.e. a type of fever patient gets profuse perspiration in the face, there is little chance of his survival.

shlokas.devanagari:
नोपैति कण्ठमाहारो जिह्वा कण्ठमुपैति च| 
आयुष्यन्तं गते जन्तोर्बलं च परिहीयते||२५||
shlokas.english: If the ingested food does not reach the throat, or the tongue falls back over the throat (thereby causing obstruction ) and there is diminution of strength, then the death of the person is imminent.

shlokas.devanagari:
शिरो विक्षिपते कृच्छ्रान्मुञ्चयित्वा प्रपाणिकौ| 
ललाटस्रुप्रतस्वेदो मुमूर्षुश्च्युतबन्धनः  ||२६||
shlokas.english: If the person moves his head with difficulty with the help of the fore-arms and if there is sweating in the forehead and is a sign of detachment from life, he is moribund.

shlokas.devanagari:
तत्र श्लोकः- 
इमानि लिङ्गानि नरेषु बुद्धिमान् विभावयेतावहितो मुमूर्षुषु| 
क्षणेन भूत्वा ह्युपयान्ति कानिचिन्नचाफलं लिङ्गमिहास्ति किञ्चन||२७||
shlokas.english: Here is the re-capitulatory verse: The wise physician should closely search for these signs repeatedly because some of them disappear in a short moment after their manifestation.

tattvaVimarsha:
The name given to this chapter, Avakshiraseeyam Indriyam (or Avakshiraseeyam Indriyam Adhyaya) may be because of the significance of the particular symptom, avakshira, which means inverted shadow of the dying person.

These moribund signs mentioned in this chapter can be classified into following types:

When a person enters the final stage of the dying process, two different dynamics are at work and are closely interrelated and interdependent. On the physical plane, the body begins the final process of shutting down, which will end when all the physical systems cease to function. Usually this is an orderly and undramatic progressive series of physical changes which are not medical emergencies requiring invasive interventions. These physical changes are a normal, natural way in which the body prepares itself for death.

The other dynamic of the dying process at work is on the emotional-spiritual psychological plane, and is a different kind of process. The spirit of the dying person begins the final process of release from the body, its immediate environment, and all attachments. This release also tends to follow its own priorities, which may include the resolution of whatever is unfinished of a practical nature and reception of permission to “let go” from family members. These events are the normal, natural way in which the spirit prepares to move from this existence into the next dimension of life. The most appropriate kinds of responses to the emotional-spiritual-psychological changes are those which support and encourage this release and transition. Some specific symptoms mentioned in this chapter are experienced and documented by people worldwide. The physician is advised to assess the moribund signs in order to stop treatment.
